narratives.Description: Passing verify:ac still prints 0 verified, 1 unverifiable with no course explanation
narratives.Overview:
## Situation

On a passing Lab 11 literal run and a passing capstone `close`, `verify:ac` printed:

```text
verify:ac passed (#3284) (0 verified, 1 unverifiable) [rung=derived]
verify:ac clause walk (#3323): 0 verified, 1 unverifiable, 0 failed
  [unverifiable] clause 1 @ (no path): The supplied focused tests and work-items CLI pass for add, complete, summary, invalid-input, and empty-collection cases without mutating input collections. — no artifact path bound
Literal acceptance-command gate passed (#3284/#3267): 2 command(s) run verbatim
```

Module 11 and the capstone teach that literal acceptance is the stored commands running verbatim and that a PASS is the required signal. They never define `verified` vs `unverifiable` clauses, `#3284`, `#3323`, or “no artifact path bound.”

The same closeout also prints `AC-pass bank checkpoint required (finalize-on-green)` and `unbounded budget — dual-stop still applies`. Dual-stop was taught in Module 9 for design-critique, not for acceptance-command banking.

## Pain

I finished the capstone with `closeout.json` `gate.status: local_pass` and still could not tell whether “0 verified, 1 unverifiable” meant a leftover defect. A mid-level engineer is being trained to treat command output as evidence. Unexplained “unverifiable” on a required passing gate makes the evidence look incomplete.

This is the same class of first-live-output surprise as Lab 2’s `vBRIEF document model` line: the course just taught a clean model, then the CLI emits a different vocabulary.

## Proposed fix

In Lab 11 and the capstone, quote this PASS fragment and classify it:

- the two stored npm commands ran and exited 0; that is the literal-acceptance proof
- `unverifiable` here means an acceptance sentence has no bound artifact path, not that the focused tests failed
- AC-pass banking and dual-stop lines are upstream 0.119.5 diagnostics; they are not capstone closeout axes

Alternatively, bind a path on the fixture acceptance clause so a passing learner run reports `1 verified, 0 unverifiable`.

## Verdict

Quoting the live `verify:ac` PASS stdout in Lab 11 and the capstone can bind. The body still needs two recuts of that identity: one quote per surface, and deletion of the bind-a-path alternative. The alternative's success criterion is false on 0.119.5.

Finding census: **0 `blocks-the-design`**, **3 `sharpens-framing`**, **2 `footnote`**.

## Re-verification of the triage anchors

Stop 1 P1 holds. Learner grep over `curriculum/`, `labs/`, `assessments/`, `solutions/`, and `references/GLOSSARY.md` has no `unverifiable`, `clause walk`, `#3284`, `#3323`, or `AC-pass bank`. The only dest hit for advisory/unverifiable is maintainer `references/SOURCE-NOTES.md` (inherited-scope clause walk on this training repo, not Lab 11).

`@deftai/directive-core@0.119.5` `dist/verify-ac/clauses.js` `walkOne`: empty `artifact_path` returns `outcome: "unverifiable"`, `detail: "no artifact path bound"`, `adjudicable: false`. `walkAcceptanceClauses.ok` is still true when `failed === 0` and no adjudicable row is unverified. `relabelVerifyAcPassLead` then prints `verify:ac passed (#3284) (0 verified, 1 unverifiable) [rung=derived]`. `maybeAttachAcPassBank` appends `AC-pass bank checkpoint required (finalize-on-green) (#3285)` and `unbounded budget — dual-stop still applies; bank is optional discipline`.

Throwaway `/tmp` probe of `walkAcceptanceClauses` against the fixture Acceptance sentences:

| case | verified | unverifiable | failed | ok | detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lab 11 unbound | 0 | 1 | 0 | true | no artifact path bound |
| capstone unbound | 0 | 1 | 0 | true | no artifact path bound |
| Lab 11 bound behavioral | 0 | 1 | 0 | true | cannot evaluate behavioral claim against shipped artifact |
| capstone bound behavioral | 0 | 1 | 0 | true | cannot evaluate behavioral claim against shipped artifact |
| existence claim bound | 1 | 0 | 0 | true | shipped artifact exists |

Lab 11 clause 1 text: `The focused test and numeric-summary CLI pass for an ordinary sample and an empty sample.` Capstone clause 1 text: `The supplied focused tests and work-items CLI pass for add, complete, summary, invalid-input, and empty-collection cases without mutating input collections.` Both fixtures stamp `plan.acceptance.source_rung: "derived"` with stated commands and `none_stated: false`. Neither fixture declares `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope` (they use `plan.metadata.file_scope`).

Helpers print only `"PASS"` to the console; the fragment lives in `literal.json.literalAcceptance.stdout` (Lab 11) and `closeout.json.gate.currentHeadGate.stdout` (capstone `task check` → `literal` → `verify:ac`).

## Findings

### F1 — sharpens-framing: quote each surface's clause 1 text

**Evidence.** The issue body gives one fenced PASS fragment whose `[unverifiable] clause 1` line is the capstone work-items Acceptance sentence. Lab 11's `story()` uses a different sentence (probe table). Lab 2 already locks live quoted evidence to what a pin-matched run prints (`scripts/verify-modules-2-3.mjs` `canonical-vendored-npm-signpost`).

**Failure mode.** Pasting that one fence into Lab 11 teaches a clause 1 line the Lab 11 runner cannot emit. Learners are trained to treat command output as evidence; a mismatched quote is false evidence.

**Disposition.** Quote Lab 11 stdout beside Task 3 / Literal acceptance commands, and capstone stdout beside literal/close. Share the classification bullets. Keep the two npm commands as the literal-acceptance proof.

### F2 — sharpens-framing: drop the bind-a-path alternative

**Evidence.** The body's alternative promises `1 verified, 0 unverifiable` after binding a path. The probe's bound-behavioral rows stay `0 verified, 1 unverifiable` because these Acceptance sentences are behavioral (#4240 in `walkOne`). `1 verified` in the probe required rewriting the clause into an existence claim. Binding also reads `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope` (`readDeclaredArtifactScope` / `#4008`); the fixtures have no such field. `clauseWalkBlocks` already treats a green executable run as the oracle for an all-unverifiable set (#3497 / #3826).

**Failure mode.** Harvest that implements the alternative will still print `unverifiable`, or will recut the Acceptance sentence into a file-existence claim and teach the wrong oracle. Adding `swarm.file_scope` would also mint a second declared-scope identity beside the course `file_scope` the helpers fingerprint.

**Disposition.** Delete the alternative from the next-build contract. The quoting identity is the one that matches the engine.

### F3 — sharpens-framing: lock the quotes the way Lab 2 locked the doctor signpost

**Evidence.** Lab 2's first-live-output recut quotes the pin-matched warning and fails the content contract if the three learner files drift (`verify-modules-2-3.mjs`). `verify-module-11.mjs` and `verify-capstone.mjs` currently lock helper verbs, evidence filenames, and `verify:ac` as a phrase; they do not lock `unverifiable`, `no artifact path bound`, or the two clause 1 sentences. Explained solutions (`solutions/lab-11-testing-gates-and-evidence.md`, `solutions/capstone-end-to-end.md`) also omit the fragment.

**Failure mode.** A later pin or Acceptance-sentence edit leaves a stale quote in the lab while the helper still prints `PASS`. That is the #19 rot shape: documented live output that the pinned engine no longer emits, or emits differently.

**Disposition.** After the per-surface quotes land, lock them in `verify-module-11.mjs` and `verify-capstone.mjs`, and classify the same fragment in the two explained solutions. Reuse Lab 2's "quoted evidence, not a step to type" fence language.

### F4 — footnote: inspect retained JSON stdout

Lab 11 `gates-lab.mjs` `main` for `literal` returns `JSON.stringify(finalStatus)` (`"PASS"`). Capstone `close` does the same. Point the quote at `literal.json` / `closeout.json` fields the issue already names, so learners do not hunt the console.

### F5 — footnote: classify `rung=derived` and the banking dual-stop line with the same bullets

`[rung=derived]` is the fixture-stamped `source_rung`, printed by `annotate` / `relabelVerifyAcPassLead`. The banking line's "dual-stop" is `evaluateAcPassBanking` note text (#3285), a different object from Module 9's design-critique dual stop. The body's third classify bullet already covers banking; fold `rung=derived` into that classification so it is not a leftover vocabulary surprise.

## Existing mechanisms

- Lab 2 quoted-evidence fences plus `verify-modules-2-3.mjs` lock (first-live-output class).
- Module 11: "A safety refusal is not a product failure and must not be relabeled as one" (classify CLI vocabulary; keep the gate).
- Lab 11 / capstone "Literal acceptance commands" sections already quote the two stored npm commands.
- GLOSSARY **literal acceptance**: stored commands ran verbatim.
- Engine: `clauseWalkBlocks` / `#3497` — green command run is the product-first oracle; unbound clauses stay advisory.

## Road not taken

Quoting versus binding a path. Binding would silence the count line only after the Acceptance sentence became an existence or quoted-token claim, and after `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope` appeared on the fixture. That recuts the taught contract and the declared-scope identity. What would flip: a `walkOne` change that marks a bound behavioral clause `verified` (reverses #4240), or an operator choice to rewrite Acceptance as existence. Neither is this recut.

## Injection / swarm lens

N/A on quoting. It fires on F2's dropped alternative: `swarm.file_scope` is the only path `walkOne` will read (#3835). Putting that field on a training fixture that already fingerprints `plan.metadata.file_scope` changes declared-scope identity. Quoting leaves that surface untouched.
